title: Counterfactual Cohort Canary for Safe Batching and KV-Prefetch Policies
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: build an experiment and canary workflow that measures counterfactual cost and quality impacts of new batching and KV-prefetch policies, provides per-cohort significance testing, and surfaces automated safe-apply/rollback recommendations in a dashboard.

Scope:
- Implement cohort assignment that preserves user-level stickiness and enables counterfactual estimation (exposed vs. synthetic control).
- Instrument telemetry for economics and quality: per-request token_cost, tokens_out, tokens_in, compute_ms, P50/P95 latency, tail errors, cache_hit_rate, and quality_delta computed against stored prompt+gold pairs.
- Provide statistical analysis pipeline: incremental sequential testing with alpha-spending, uplift estimators (ATE & IPW where applicable), and bias diagnostics (covariate balance tables).
- Build Grafana dashboard with: cohort-level metrics, rolling-stat windows (1h/24h/7d), statistical annotations (p-value, uplift CI), automated safety flags and recommended rollback action.
- Implement safe-apply orchestration: preflight checks, canary quota, automated rollback trigger on safety gates, and post-rollback mitigation steps.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cohort assignment service returns stable cohort_id for 99.9% of requests within 5s.
- Analysis pipeline produces per-cohort uplift and a decision label (SAFE / REVIEW / ROLLBACK) within 10 minutes of 10k events.
- Dashboard contains visualizations for cost per 1k tokens, SLA (P95 latency) delta, cache hit delta, quality regression (A/B test on evaluation prompts), and a summary rollback recommendation box.
- Automated rollback fires when any of the top-3 safety gates breach thresholds for >5 minutes and correctly routes 100% of affected traffic to baseline model variant.

Metrics and key signals we will track:
- Economic: tokens_out_per_request, compute_cost_per_request ($ estimate), effective throughput (req/s).
- Latency/Reliability: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, error_rate_5xx, tail_latency_99_ms.
- Cache/batching: kv_cache_hit_rate, avg_microbatch_size, batching_delay_ms.
- Quality: eval_set_accuracy_delta, semantic_sim_score_delta (embedding cosine), human-sampled quality score.
- Safety gates: cost_increase_pct (vs baseline), latency_p95_increase_pct, quality_regression_pct, error_rate_increase_pct.

Analysis details (implementation notes):
- Use instrumentation events exported to our analytics pipeline (kafka->warehouse). Provide SQL recipes for uplift and IPW estimators (stored as notebooks).
- Use sequential analysis with O'Brien-Fleming style alpha spending to allow early stopping without inflating Type I.
- Provide stratified results by customer_tier, region, request_type (streaming vs. non-streaming), and prompt_length_bucket.
- Implement counterfactual scoring for requests not routed to experiment using model-simulated cost estimates (baseline model run on a sample) to enable cost uplift estimates when routing capacity is constrained.

Rollback policy (automated):
1) Safety gate evaluation runs every 60s.
2) If any gate breaches configured threshold for >5min, mark cohort as ROLLBACK_CANDIDATE and start graceful rollback (drain new config, route traffic to baseline).
3) Post-rollback validations: sanity checks on 200 random requests and reconciliation of token billing.
4) Create incident ticket with summary and attach diagnostic snapshots.

Operational runbook links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Counterfactual+Cohort+Canary+Design
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/-cost/counterfactual-canary-v1
- Analysis notebook: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/experiments/notebooks/counterfactual_analysis.ipynb
- PR for cohort service: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1234

Notes on privacy and data retention: only store prompt identifiers and hashed user ids in the analysis dataset. Evaluation prompts are stored in a separate locked table with 90-day retention.
